## Summary

Define composition and its inverse

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
$part ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) $container;

Relation//CONTAINS ((IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR)) Relation//IS_CONTAINED_BY;

alias(Relation//IS_CONTAINED_BY) == "+>";

alias(Relation//CONTAINS) == "/";

Relation//IS_CONTAINED_BY ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

The Target has classification `Container = yes`.

## Semantics

IS_CONTAINED_BY relates a declared Entity or instance to its immediate Container. CONTAINS is its inverse alias; both writings identify the same fact. `Whole/Part` writes the inverse view and `Part +> Whole` the canonical direction. Containment does not imply narrowing or inheritance.

## Summary

Declare SPECIALIZES

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//IS_SPECIALIZED_BY ((IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR)) Relation//SPECIALIZES;

Relation//SPECIALIZES ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct;

# instances
$specializing_atom[<Atom>] ((SPECIALIZES)) $specialized_atom[<Atom>]
```

### Prose Claim

The child Atom's Claim is more specific or stricter than the parent Atom's Claim in the same or a narrower Scope and preserves the parent's applicable constraints. A conditional specialization is included. A reference or dependency alone does not establish SPECIALIZES. IS_SPECIALIZED_BY is the inverse alias, with parent and child endpoints reversed.

## Semantics

SPECIALIZES relates a child Atom to the Atom whose Claim it specializes.

## Summary

Define Relation alias syntax with `alias($r)`

## Claim

### Prose Claim

`alias($r) == "notation token"` takes an already-bound Relation participant, such as one selected by `$r[<Relation>, (.Name = RELATION_NAME)]`, and binds that declared graph Relation’s exact name to one nonempty lexical notation token in the selected effective MODEL. Resolve the name exactly; do not infer case folding or undeclared synonyms. A Relation has at most one authored alias. Reject undeclared Relation names, conflicting alias values, and ambiguous token bindings. Without an alias, use the full named Relation notation.

This syntax binds notation metadata; it does not construct a graph Relation fact or equate different Relation identities. The token follows the owning Relation Declaration’s directional reading and grants no endpoint permission, cardinality, or second authored fact. In a graph expression, an already-bound Relation participant references that Relation object as an endpoint, whereas `((NAME))` invokes that Relation between endpoints.

## Summary

Define Relation alias syntax with `alias($r)`

## Claim

### Prose Claim

`alias(Relation//NAME) == "notation token"` binds one nonempty lexical notation token to a canonical Relation model name or its inverse alias model name. Resolve the name exactly; do not infer case folding or undeclared synonyms. Each written name has at most one authored short notation token. Reject unknown names, conflicting alias values and ambiguous token bindings. Without a short token, use the full named Relation notation.

A token follows its written name's directional reading. This notation is metadata, not a graph Relation fact; it grants no endpoint permission or cardinality and creates no second Relation fact or Alias entity. Fixed names are written `Relation//NAME`; `((NAME))` invokes the corresponding Relation writing between endpoints.

## Summary

Define Relation

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation;

Relation.** {::1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) (Relation, Relation.**);
(Relation, Relation.**) {::0+}((HAS_PROPERTY)) Relation.**;

# instances
$relation[<Relation>];
$relation.** {::1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) ($relation, $relation.**);
($relation, $relation.**) {::0+}((HAS_PROPERTY)) $relation.**;
```

### Prose Claim

Relation defines a reusable directed graph Relation Type with a Name and Meaning. Each actual link is a tuple (Host, Relation Type, Target); persist each direct fact once. An actual edge does not create a separate Relation ID. Endpoints are declared model Entities or instances, including Carrier and Relation descriptors, except that HAS_ALLOWED_VALUE and HAS_VALUE_CONSTRAINT have literal or constraint-data Targets, and their declared derived inverses have those data as Hosts. CFEL glyphs are not endpoints. CFEL syntax does not itself create an endpoint.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning, endpoint signature and any counterpart binding. A derived counterpart remains a distinct Relation with its own Declaration; its meaning and endpoints are inferred through that binding. An alias supplies lexical notation for one Relation; it does not create a new Relation, a Node or a separate Relation ID.

## Summary

Declare IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
$host ((IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR)) $target
```

### Prose Claim

IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR binds an inverse alias model address to its canonical Relation model address. The inverse alias is introduced by the canonical Relation Declaration and is not a separate Relation entity or Declaration. Normalizing an inverse alias to its canonical Relation swaps the written endpoints and their cardinality slots, preserving the numeric bounds. Explicit reverse writing of an inverse alias reverses its endpoints and slots again. Both writings refer to the same fact. This binding infers no bounds, grants no endpoint permission and creates no second authored Relation fact.

## Semantics

IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR relates an inverse alias address to its canonical Relation address.
